newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish PM says longer trend factor in ERM link.
newsitem.headline: Finnish PM says longer trend factor in ERM link.

text.p: The markka's possible entry into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) will be at a combination of its spot rate and a longer-term average, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen was quoted as telling a Finnish newspaper on Wednesday.

"He detailed...that the central parity rate for the markka in ERM will not be simply the current market exchange rate, but the average exchange rate over a period of time will also be taken into account," daily Hufvudstadsbladet reported.
"A longer trend will be considered," Lipponen was quoted by the newspaper as saying.

The Bank of Finland intervened in markets on Tuesday, selling markka for German marks amid mounting speculation that Finland may decide this weekend to link its currency to the stability mechanism, foreign exchange dealers said.
The markka had started rising sharply on Monday after Lipponen told another newspaper the time was ripe for a decision in the near future on a markka-ERM link.
Lipponen also said there would be no scope for manipulation of the exchange rate when fixing the central parity rate for the markka.

Some analysts said on Monday the right time to link the markka, which has been floating since 1992, could be in connection with the coming weekend's meeting of EU finance and economy ministers in Dublin.
The central bank's activity failed to stop a rising trend in the Finnish currency, which closed on Tuesday at a four-week high of 2.9975 against the German mark.
